title: The Close constellation — the project's knowledge network
_doc: PROPOSED (2026-07-22, awaiting Sérgio) — the target shape for data/strings/close_network.json, which is today a flat list of 24 hand-typed labels. The Close's point cloud is canonically 'symbolically drawn from the data/connections used to make this immersive experience itself' (master plan F6) and its hub nodes carry 'the network of knowledge the piece itself is built from' (src/room/pointCloud.ts). Today the mesh's TOPOLOGY does not honour that: node positions are seeded-random, links join near neighbours by spatial proximity only, and labels are assigned to whichever nodes happened to render largest. This schema makes the network real. NOTHING has been migrated — see the criteria doc and Sérgio's approval before data moves. THE ETHICS RULE THAT SHAPES THIS FILE: a node's visible `label` is ALWAYS authored, never copied from a dossier source's `text`, because those texts name real people and legal cases while this surface's own standing rule is 'No survivor names, no real individuals — sources and structures only.' Derivation supplies structure and status; wording stays Sérgio's.

sergioPass.description: FALSE until Sérgio's wording/ethics pass. While false, nodes with status 'unrated' are REPORTED by tools/check-spec.mjs. The moment it is true, any 'unrated' node is a hard CI failure — the flag is the whole gate, so it is the only thing he has to flip.

nodes.description: The stars. Two populations merged: 'authored' (the PhD frame, ethics constraints, research passes — things no code can infer) and 'derived' (dossier sources already carrying a status). A derived node's identity and status come from the build; only its label is human.

id.description: stable slug — edges reference it, so renaming a label never breaks the graph

label.description: THE VISIBLE TEXT, always authored by Sérgio. Never auto-filled from a source's `text` field (see the ethics rule in _doc). A derived node awaiting a label carries the empty string and is reported, not invented.

origin.description: 'derived' nodes are regenerated from data/provotypes/*.json debrief sources and must not be hand-edited except for their label; 'authored' nodes are Sérgio's and are never touched by tooling.

status.description: Same vocabulary as the dossier law (CLAUDE.md), because these ARE those sources. Intended to drive node BRIGHTNESS in the Close: documentary burns bright, contested dimmer, speculative faintest — the honesty of the research becomes the last image the player sees, and the piece closes by admitting what it does not know. 'unrated' is a pre-pass sentinel only, legal while sergioPass is false.

confidence.description: player-visible confidence label, carried over from the dossier source where one exists

kind.description: 'source' = documentary anchor; 'research' = a deep-research pass; 'scene' = a provotype/beat the sources ground; 'frame' = the PhD/project frame (SurvivingSOGICE, ethics constraints). Hubs should be frame + heavily-cited sources.

verified.description: false where the source text still carries [VERIFY SOURCE]. An unverified node must never render as a bright documentary star — that would be the piece's own uncited claim, in its final image.

edges.description: The web. ONLY relations that are already RECORDED somewhere in the build — writing them down asserts nothing new. The generative case: source S appears in provotype P's debrief ⇒ S grounds P. Interpretive links between sources ('NARTH influenced GETA') are research claims and belong to Sérgio, never to a generator.

relation.description: 'grounds' = this source is cited by that scene (derivable, non-interpretive); 'informs' = a research pass fed this scene; 'supersedes' = one decision replaced another — the relation that would have caught the R28-versus-shipped drift, and the reason this graph doubles as the tracking system the 84 docs never gave us.

origin.description: as for nodes — derived edges are regenerated and must not be hand-edited
